clue.text: Graduate regrettably turning back in greeting

indicators.note: turning back tells us to read the whole run of letters from the far end

parts.note: MA, Master of Arts, is a graduate's degree
alas is said regrettably, an exclamation of sorrow

explanation.surface: A new graduate sadly turns away while saying hello.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning back' reverses MA + ALAS together, giving SALAAM.
explanation.definitionFit: A salaam is a respectful Eastern salutation with a low bow, so it is a form of greeting.

clue.text: Fruit a naval commander identifies

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for commanding officer
RN, Royal Navy, stands in for naval

explanation.surface: A naval officer recognises a piece of fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces come in the order A, CO, RN, not the order the clue gives them; 'identifies' is the link.
explanation.definitionFit: The acorn is the nut-like fruit of the oak tree.

clue.text: Living extremely lavishly in the long term

parts.note: abiding can mean living or dwelling, as in abiding in a place

indicators.note: extremely asks for the extremes, the first and last letters, of lavishly

explanation.surface: Someone lives in grand style, in luxury for good.
explanation.definitionFit: Abidingly means lastingly or enduringly, so it covers what holds in the long term.

clue.text: Servant carrying fish over

indicators.note: carrying means the servant word holds the fish word inside it

parts.note: a man is a manservant
the ide is a freshwater fish, a crossword regular

explanation.surface: A servant brings fish across the room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' looks like a direction for the fish, but it is the definition, a cricket term.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket, a maiden is an over of six balls from which no runs are scored.

clue.text: Dessert unfinished, start to study course outline

indicators.note: unfinished asks for the dessert word to lose its final letter

parts.note: a syllabub is a creamy whipped pudding

indicators.note: start to points at the opening letter of study

explanation.surface: Someone half-eats a pudding before starting work on the course plan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unfinished' cuts the last B from SYLLABUB, leaving SYLLABU; S from 'start to study' completes it.
explanation.definitionFit: A syllabus is an outline listing the topics a course of study covers.

clue.text: Camel floating across the sand?

definitions.meaning: the desert beast of burden with a hump
a whimsical picture of a vessel sailing over dunes, the camel's rolling gait likened to a boat on waves

explanation.surface: A camel seems to glide over the desert.
explanation.definitionFit: Ship of the desert is a long-standing nickname for the camel, the transport of desert travel.

clue.text: Play about with minute cairn, possibly

indicators.note: about means the play word goes around the other pieces

parts.note: to lark is to play about, fool around
and is a synonym of with, joining things

explanation.surface: Someone fools around briefly with a pile of stones.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Play' reads as a verb but is the noun-like lark that 'about' wraps round the rest; 'possibly' warns that a cairn is only one example of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A cairn is a heap of stones that marks a summit or path, so it is one kind of guiding feature.

clue.text: Fossilised resin found in Cookham, Berks

indicators.note: found in says the answer sits inside the letters of the following place name

explanation.surface: A fossil has turned up in a Berkshire village.
explanation.walkthrough: COOKHAM is a village in Berkshire, England, and 'Berks' is that county's short form.
explanation.definitionFit: Amber is tree resin that has hardened over millions of years, a fossil gum.

clue.text: Blatant imposture defended by people of both sexes

indicators.note: defended by means the imposture word is guarded on both sides by the people

parts.note: Una is a woman's name
Ed is a man's name
a sham is a pretence or imposture

explanation.surface: A brazen fraud is protected by men and women alike.
explanation.walkthrough: 'people of both sexes' is one woman's name and one man's name, the imposture sitting between them as 'defended by' says, as though guarded on both flanks.
explanation.definitionFit: Unashamed behaviour is shown openly without embarrassment, which is what blatant means.

clue.text: Legislator a woman artist referred to in speech

indicators.note: referred to in speech says the words are judged by their spoken form

parts.note: Polly is a woman's name and Titian was the Venetian painter

explanation.surface: A lawmaker mentions a female painter in an address.
explanation.walkthrough: POLLY TITIAN said out loud is POLITICIAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A politician is one who makes laws, such as a member of a parliament.

clue.text: Harsh cry from the vicar's place

definitions.meaning: the loud call of a donkey
the parish of the time-serving vicar in the old song The Vicar of ...

explanation.surface: A loud shout comes from the parsonage.
explanation.walkthrough: The Vicar of Bray is an 18th-century English song about a clergyman who changed his beliefs to keep his living.
explanation.definitionFit: A bray is the harsh cry of a donkey, and Bray is a Berkshire parish famous from the song.

clue.text: Leander was not the central character

definitions.text: Leander was not the central character

parts.words: Leander was not the central character
parts.note: in Greek myth Leander swam the Hellespont nightly to his lover Hero, so Leander was not Hero; read straight it describes a lead figure without heroic qualities

explanation.surface: A lover from Greek legend was not the main figure of the story.
explanation.definitionFit: An antihero is a central character in a story who lacks heroic qualities such as courage.

clue.text: Drive over pitch? It's waterlogged

indicators.note: over means the drive word is turned backwards

parts.note: to ram is to drive, as a post into the ground
to shy is to throw or pitch

explanation.surface: A golfer hits a drive over a pitch that turns out to be flooded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' reverses RAM to MAR. 'pitch' tempts as a football field, but it means throw.
explanation.definitionFit: Marshy ground is soft and wet like a marsh, saturated with water.

clue.text: Self-satisfied, giving sweets back

indicators.note: back says the sweets word is read in reverse

parts.note: gums are chewy sweets such as wine gums

explanation.surface: A complacent person hands back the sweets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' reverses GUMS.
explanation.definitionFit: Smug describes someone excessively pleased with themselves, complacent.

clue.text: Philosopher hit on revised ordinal

parts.note: John Stuart Mill was the English philosopher

indicators.note: revised says the letters of hit on are reworked into a new order

explanation.surface: A thinker comes up with a new version of a numbering idea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revised' rearranges the letters of hit on into IONTH, which follows the philosopher's surname.
explanation.definitionFit: An ordinal number gives a position in a series, and one-millionth is such a position.

clue.text: Irritating storms regularly disrupting Scottish island

indicators.note: disrupting means the picked letters break into the island's name

parts.note: Tiree is an island in the Inner Hebrides

indicators.note: regularly asks for every other letter of storms, starting with the first

explanation.surface: Annoying gales keep cutting off a Hebridean island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes the odd letters of storms; 'disrupting' puts them before the final E of the island, which lies off Scotland's west coast.
explanation.definitionFit: Something tiresome is wearying and annoying, so it is irritating.

clue.text: Real thugs prepared to kill

indicators.note: prepared means the letters of real thugs are made ready in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Genuine hoodlums are ready to commit murder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'prepared' rearranges REALTHUGS; 'to' is the link.
explanation.definitionFit: To slaughter is to kill, especially brutally or in great numbers.

clue.text: Male lyrist who controls dreams?

parts.note: Orpheus was the legendary Greek player of the lyre

explanation.surface: A musician with a lyre seems to be master of sleep visions.
explanation.definitionFit: Morpheus is the Greek god of dreams, who shapes the visions of sleepers.

clue.text: Sticky earth in greater quantity? It's mine

parts.note: clay is stiff, sticky soil
more means a greater amount

explanation.surface: Someone claims a larger heap of mud as their own.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mine' looks like the possessive, but it is the explosive device; 'It's' is the link.
explanation.definitionFit: The Claymore is a directional anti-personnel mine, named after the Scottish broadsword.

clue.text: An Indian oddly in title role

indicators.note: oddly picks the letters in odd positions of Indian: first, third, fifth

explanation.surface: An Indian actor oddly lands the lead part.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly' gives I, D, A from Indian, after A from 'An'.
explanation.definitionFit: Aida is the Ethiopian princess who is the title role of Verdi's opera.

clue.text: A European king ousted by duke? That's right

indicators.note: ousted by means one letter is thrown out and another takes its place

parts.note: a Greek is a European from Greece

explanation.surface: A monarch from Europe is overthrown by a nobleman, and everyone agrees.
explanation.walkthrough: 'king' is K and 'duke' is D, the standard chess and peerage short forms: 'ousted by' swaps K in GREEK for D, giving GREED.
explanation.definitionFit: Agreed! is said as an interjection of assent, meaning that's right, I concur.

clue.text: Sound fellow shot in the arm

indicators.note: Sound says the fellow's name is taken by how it is spoken

parts.note: Philip is a man's name, any fellow

explanation.surface: A healthy man is given an injection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sound' looks like 'healthy', describing the fellow, but it signals PHILIP said out loud.
explanation.definitionFit: A fillip is a stimulus or boost, figuratively a shot in the arm.

clue.text: Resinous substance coating the Italian shrub

indicators.note: coating means the resin word wraps around the Italian word

parts.note: lac is the resin secreted by insects, used in shellac
il is the Italian for the

explanation.surface: Resin is painted over a shrub from Italy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coating' has the resin go round the Italian article; lac is the raw form of shellac.
explanation.definitionFit: The lilac is a garden shrub with fragrant purple or white flowers.

clue.text: Attractive, holding fast

definitions.meaning: gripping or interlocking, as gears mesh and grip

explanation.surface: A charming person keeps a firm grip.
explanation.definitionFit: Engaging means charming, and gears engaging lock together, holding fast.

clue.text: Railwaymen have points to look after

parts.note: NUR was the National Union of Railwaymen in Britain
S and E are compass points, south and east

explanation.surface: Railway workers have signal points to maintain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'points' tempts as railway points, but means compass points; 'have' and 'to' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: To nurse is to tend or care for someone, to look after them.

clue.text: It produces dye by a river out East

indicators.note: out means the letter for East is taken away

parts.note: the Nile is the great African river

explanation.surface: A dye plant grows by an Eastern river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' removes E from ANILE; 'by' is the link.
explanation.definitionFit: Anil is the indigo shrub, a plant from which the blue dye is obtained.

clue.text: Simple, yet real crazy about blokes

indicators.note: about means the rearranged letters go around the blokes word
crazy says the letters of yet real are jumbled

parts.note: blokes means men, British slang

explanation.surface: Someone is plain, yet genuinely mad about men.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crazy' turns the letters of yet real into ELETARY; 'about' wraps it round the blokes, which split it after ELE.
explanation.definitionFit: Elementary means basic and straightforward, so simple.

clue.text: Stocky group of pupils with little promise

parts.note: a thick pupil, dim-witted, shows little promise
a set is a group of pupils taught together by ability

explanation.surface: A sturdy class of students shows few signs of talent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' is the link; in British schools a set is a class grouped by ability.
explanation.definitionFit: Thickset describes someone heavily built and solid, stocky.

clue.text: Light dinner to start with seafood

indicators.note: to start with picks the opening letter of dinner

parts.note: an ormer is an edible shellfish, the abalone

explanation.surface: A light meal begins with shellfish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Light' looks like an adjective for the dinner, but it is the window.
explanation.definitionFit: A dormer is a window set upright in a sloping roof, a source of light.
